candidates.name: Stargardt disease
support_spans: symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea
attenuated photopic responses and 30-Hz flicker responses with delayed implicit times in both eyes
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results are consistent with Stargardt disease, a juvenile macular degeneration disorder.

candidates.name: Stargardt disease
support_spans: Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging demonstrated symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea, partial preservation of the ellipsoid zone, and a normal retinal nerve fiber layer
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including FAF and OCT results, are consistent with Stargardt disease

candidates.name: Cone-rod dystrophy
support_spans: Full-field electroretinography (ff-ERG) revealed normal scotopic responses but attenuated photopic responses and 30-Hz flicker responses with delayed implicit times in both eyes
candidates.why: The patient's ff-ERG results, showing normal scotopic but attenuated photopic responses, are consistent with cone-rod dystrophy

candidates.name: Retinitis pigmentosa
support_spans: ff-ERG showed delayed implicit times in the dark-adapted 0.01 ERG, an electronegative waveform in the dark-adapted 3.0 ERG, and non-recordable photopic and 30-Hz flicker responses in both eyes
candidates.why: The patient's father's ff-ERG results, showing delayed implicit times and non-recordable photopic responses, are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa
